title: ScalarField derives by excluding arrays, not by testing for string
context: src/domain/spine.ts carried a hand-written ScalarField union and SCALAR_CAP table that did not know about landed, so the writer's cap check never fired and the schema's own limit became the only guard, with a different refusal shape than every other spine scalar. The plan said to derive the union from the Spine type if cheap. The first derivation was written as Spine[K] extends string ? K : never.
options: Keep the hand-written union and add landed to it
Derive as Spine[K] extends string ? K : never
Derive by exclusion as Spine[K] extends unknown[] ? never : K
outcome: Derived by exclusion. The extends-string form has a silent hole: a future string-or-null field resolves to never, drops out of the cap table and gets no cap check, reintroducing exactly the defect the derivation existed to close. The inverted form makes a nullable field demand its cap loudly instead. Confirmed with a scratchpad tsc probe: the old form exits 0 on a nullable field, the new one exits 2 naming the missing key. CollectionField was derived alongside it, since it is the same mapped type and closes the identical drift.
